title: Thirteen-link calc bounding f/Δ for polynomially-growing Fourier coefficients
intent: Prove the blueprint's Lemma 7.4 (an upper bound on the ratio of a function with polynomially-growing Fourier coefficients to the modular discriminant Δ) as one monotone calc chain, one private step lemma per link, so each factor of the product (leading exponential, sum of coefficient norms, infinite product) is bounded by its own small lemma.

parent.name: DivDiscBoundOfPolyFourierCoeff
parent.statement:
theorem DivDiscBoundOfPolyFourierCoeff : norm ((f z) / (Δ z)) ≤
  (DivDiscBound c n₀) * rexp (-π * (n₀ - 2) * z.im)

children.name: step_1
children.statement: norm (f z / Δ z) = norm ((∑' n, c (n+n₀) * cexp (π*I*(n+n₀)*z)) / (cexp (2*π*I*z) * ∏' n : ℕ+, (1 - cexp (2*π*I*n*z))^24)) — unfold f via hf/fouterm and Δ via DiscriminantProductFormula

children.name: step_2
children.statement: pull cexp (π*I*n₀*z) out of the tsum: ∑' n, c (n+n₀) * cexp (π*I*(n+n₀)*z) = cexp (π*I*n₀*z) * ∑' n, c (n+n₀) * cexp (π*I*n*z)
children.closed_by: congr; rw [← tsum_mul_left]; ext n; ring_nf; rw [mul_assoc, ← Complex.exp_add]; ring

children.name: step_3
children.statement: fold cexp (π*I*n₀*z) into the numerator as the quotient cexp (π*I*n₀*z) / cexp (2*π*I*z)

children.name: step_5
children.statement: norm (a * b / c) = norm a * norm b / norm c, pushing norm through the product and division

children.name: step_6
children.statement: norm (∏' n : ℕ+, (1 - cexp (2*π*I*n*z))^24) = ∏' n : ℕ+, norm (1 - cexp (2*π*I*n*z))^24

children.name: step_7
children.statement: norm (cexp (π*I*(n₀-2)*z)) ≤ rexp (-π*(n₀-2)*z.im) — the first inequality, bounding the leading exponential
children.closed_by: gcongr; exact aux_6 z; norm_cast; exact aux_7 z (n₀-2)

children.name: step_8
children.statement: norm (∑' n, c (n+n₀) * cexp (π*I*n*z)) ≤ ∑' n, norm (c (n+n₀)) * norm (cexp (π*I*n*z)) — triangle inequality for the infinite sum
children.closed_by: norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm; aux_3 z c n₀ hcsum

children.name: step_9
children.statement: norm (cexp (π*I*n*z)) = rexp (-π*n*z.im) pointwise, so the sum becomes ∑' n, norm (c (n+n₀)) * rexp (-π*n*z.im)

children.name: step_10
children.statement: ∏' n : ℕ+, norm (1 - cexp (2*π*I*n*z))^24 ≤ ∏' n : ℕ+, (1 - rexp (-2*π*n*z.im))^24 — bound each product factor below the denominator

children.name: step_11
children.statement: ∑' n, norm (c (n+n₀)) * rexp (-π*n*z.im) ≤ ∑' n, norm (c (n+n₀)) * rexp (-π*n/2) — the polynomial-growth step, using z.im > 1/2 and hpoly

children.name: step_12
children.statement: ∏' n : ℕ+, (1 - rexp (-2*π*n*z.im))^24 ≤ ∏' n : ℕ+, (1 - rexp (-π*n))^24 — bound the product using z.im > 1/2

children.name: step_13
children.statement: the final expression equals (DivDiscBound c n₀) * rexp (-π*(n₀-2)*z.im) — recognise the definition of DivDiscBound

applicability.goal_shape: A bound norm (g z) ≤ C * r z (or an equality/inequality chain between quotients of norms, exponentials and infinite sums/products) that factors into a leading exponential, a sum of norms and an infinite product, each factor boundable by its own lemma.
applicability.use_when: the bound factors into independent pieces so each can be bounded by one lemma, and the whole is a monotone =/≤ chain; the informal proof (blueprint or paper) is already a displayed = ≤ = ≤ = chain; each link is a clean standalone statement whose endpoints definitionally match the adjacent links.
applicability.avoid_when: a step needs too much local context to state standalone (keep it as an inline `have`/`calc`); the chain is short enough that one `calc` with `rw`/`gcongr` inline is clearer than many one-use lemmas; the children have no independent interest and are pure rewrites.

consequences: Thirteen private lemmas, one per link, stated before the theorem and referenced by name; transitivity of the chain is checked by `calc` itself, so each child's only obligation is that its two endpoints definitionally match the adjacent links (its LHS must equal the previous link's RHS). Failure modes: a child whose statement drifts from the chain endpoints will not elaborate; a one-use child that cannot be stated cleanly (needs many section variables, as step_11 includes hz hcsum hpoly) is boilerplate; and a missing summability hypothesis (hcsum in step_8, step_9, step_11) silently fails the chain.
